pr_snapshot.body:
`dsp.SAD16x16Limit` still routed through the generic limited-SAD dispatcher after the fixed 16×16 pointer kernels were optimized. Route eligible slice calls through those existing kernels, preserving exact row-prefix results and the scalar backend’s visible-slice bounds checks. Production change: three lines.

Native Apple M4 Max, Go 1.27.2 SIMD, PGO off, six fresh permutations against current main and pinned assembly:

- All 20 public slice-caller cases improve versus main in every pair, with zero allocations. Early exits improve **1.592–1.601×**; every early pair exceeds 1.5× (minimum 1.576×). Full/wide scans improve 1.418–1.428×.
- Full/wide scans are 2.547–2.576× faster than the equivalent assembly slice API. Early exits are approximately tied with assembly (0.994–1.005×).
- Whole VP8 remains mixed: 300 frames +0.151% time versus main (3/6 faster), 60 frames −0.734% (3/6 faster). Current still takes 4.811%/11.734% more time than assembly in these windows. All 23 non-timing fields match; zero allocations. Retain the verified component win independently of whole-codec timing; no general ARM-gap closure claimed.

Full native tests pass. Focused validation includes 11 native SAD tests with race/checkptr2, 14 AMD Rosetta correctness tests with checkptr2, actual AMD AVX-off fallback checks, and purego/nosimd checks. New tests cover 416 exact scalar comparisons and 45 short visible-header cases, including independent source/reference one-byte boundaries. PGO profile/fingerprint and source/build-selection gates pass.

Extend native AMD CI with the same 20-case B.Loop fixture on assembly/main/current (134 total kernel cases). AMD generated code retains an internal dispatch call boundary; Rosetta provides correctness evidence only. Fresh native x64 CI results follow; keep them separate from the ARM figures above.

Native EPYC 7763, Go 1.27.2, PGO off, six paired rounds versus main `a6eec452` and old assembly `691cd051`:
- All 20 new public slice-SAD cases improve versus main in every pair. Full/wide bounds improve 2.018–2.046x, with every pair at least 2.014x. Early bounds improve 1.498–1.502x by the ratio of medians, but the minimum individual pair is 1.385x; these early cases do not meet 1.5x in every pair. Middle improves 1.006–1.169x and near 1.016–1.039x. Eight full/wide fixtures exceed 1.5x in every pair.
- Full/wide slice cases take 8.69–8.86% less time than assembly. Early/middle/near still take 24.74–80.69% more time. The older `BenchmarkSAD16x16LimitEarly` improves 1.650x versus main (all pairs at least 1.644x), resolving its preceding main-relative regression; it still takes 21.273% more time than assembly.
- Whole VP8 is +0.449% time versus main (2/6 faster), VP9 320 -0.572% (4/6), VP9 720 -1.013% (3/6). They take 13.277%/39.486%/46.461% less time than assembly respectively on this CPU. Whole results remain mixed and do not close previously observed gaps on ARM or other x64 CPUs. Short profiles do not establish a material whole-codec contribution from the slice dispatcher.
- The 20 unchanged pointer-SAD controls range -0.149% to +0.289% versus main. Preserve all 62 median-regressing kernels; the only all-six-slower control is Variance16x16 +0.213%. Largest median control drift is picker pitch32/mixed +0.888% (4/6 slower).
- All 134 kernel cases have six samples per variant and zero B/op/allocs. Targeted native validation passes 75 top-level tests plus six retained panic child probes (81 checks; 103 PASS lines including older subtests), no failures/skips, with main/current SIMD dispatch confirmed. All 22 semantic fields match across three public and two profile datasets. Every allocation sample matches; no allocation outliers this run.

The separate optimized-libvpx job runs on EPYC 9V74 with pinned v1.16.0, runtime dispatch, SSE2/AVX2 and assembly objects enabled. Fixed-speed VP8 takes 2.445x libvpx time (13.097 versus 5.357 ms/input), with matching measured PSNR, SSIM, payload size and encoded/dropped counts; this does not assert bitstream identity. Adaptive VP8 is +83.612% and VP9 +178.365%/+189.335%, with unequal quality/output work. Every quality-pass output statistic matches timed output; reference timing uses vpxenc statistics. No cross-job absolute comparison or source attribution is made.

All three exact-head CI checks pass. Raw artifacts: [native](https://github.com/thesyncim/govpx/actions/runs/39064601549/artifacts/12112763932), [optimized C](https://github.com/thesyncim/govpx/actions/runs/39064601549/artifacts/12113330049).

Preserve PR30’s complete native/C audit and all regressions: unchanged-source EPYC 9V74 controls still show VP8 12.043% slower than assembly, while VP9 is 41.061%/48.141% faster. Separate EPYC 9V45 fixed VP8 takes 2.174× optimized libvpx time at matching measured quality/payload/counts. Also archive the unselected goav1 wide-statistics experiments. Raw samples, source snapshots, correctness and codegen live in dated baseline directories. README unchanged.
